values.note: Clark's own page: 'Family Campground - $22 per site per night'. The statewide first-come table reads $12 non-electric, $12.15 primitive; the forest's page is the one naming this campground.

fees.source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/forestry/properties/clark-state-forest/ ('Family Campground - $22 per site per night'), read 2026-11-02

values.note: Pit toilets and water in the campground. The shower house and dump station are in the equestrian campground, across I-65, for paid campers of both; dump free to them.

facilities.source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/forestry/properties/clark-state-forest/ ('There are pit toilets and a water supply located throughout each campground'; 'The comfort station for both campgrounds is in the equestrian campground'; 'The dump station ... is free to paid camping customers'), read 2026-11-02

sites.source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/forestry/properties/clark-state-forest/ ('It offers 40 individual campsites, each with a picnic table and fire ring'), read 2026-11-02

values.note: Self-register at the forest office, 2 Service Road, Henryville: cash or check in an envelope, then clip the receipt to the site marker.

booking.source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/forestry/properties/clark-state-forest/ ('available on a first-come, first-served basis'; 'All campers are required to self-register and pay at the Clark State Forest main office'), read 2026-11-02

note: Indiana DNR Division of Forestry, Clark State Forest family campground, just east of I-65 off Winding Road. Seven small lakes on the property but sites are not on a shore. (Separate equestrian campground excluded.) --Claude
summary: Fee $12-12.15 -> $22 (the forest's own page names this campground; statewide table disagrees, flagged). 40 sites, no electric, FCFS confirmed. Added pit toilets, water, showers and dump (both in the horse camp). Pin 1.2 km off. Not waterfront stands.
flags: FEE CONFLICT: Clark's page says 'Family Campground - $22 per site per night'; the statewide first-come table says non-electric $12, primitive $12.15. Wrote $22. Neither page is dated. A call to 812-294-4306 would settle it.

PIN: stored 38.553,-85.7669 is the forest's front gate/office on US 31 (Google's point for the whole forest, 38.55296,-85.76687). DNR's brochure map puts 'Family Campground' just east of I-65, north of Service Rd. Imagery shows a gravel loop around a clearing there. Correct to about 38.5608,-85.7766, about 1.2 km NW. I can see the loop road, not individual pads.
FIT: DNR gives no length or RV statement for this campground; wording is not singled out. No review naming a rig was read. Google's listing (4.6 from 788) is the whole forest.
ADVISORIES read 2026-11-02: only a Knobstone Trail section and the fire tower closed; nothing on the campground.
SEASON not written: page says the toilets and water 'are available year-round', and the comfort station has a winter bathroom, but no sentence says the campground itself is open year-round.
WATER: not waterfront stands. Nearest water on imagery is Schlamm Lake, west of I-65, or Oak Lake to the south: none beside the clearing. Overpass timed out, so imagery only.
